items.title: Layla Buys Oranges in Marrakesh
items.summary: Layla shops for fruit and bread at the busy market in Marrakesh.
items.body: Layla goes to the big market in Marrakesh every Friday. She buys sweet oranges, warm bread, and red apples. The market is very busy. People sell colorful shoes and small lamps. Layla talks with a friendly seller and he gives her one orange for free. She smiles and says thank you. At home, she makes cold orange juice for her family.

words.def: a place where people buy and sell things
with many people and much activity
a basic food made from flour

questions.q: Where does Layla buy food?
questions.a: At the big market in Marrakesh.

questions.q: What does the seller give Layla for free?
What does Layla make for her family?

items.title: A Rainy Walk for Tom
items.summary: Tom enjoys a quiet rainy day with hot chocolate in a London cafe.
items.body: Tom lives in London. It is raining today, so he takes his black umbrella. He walks to the small cafe near his house. Inside, the cafe is warm and quiet. Tom drinks hot chocolate and reads a book about birds. He watches the rain through the window. Tom likes rainy days because the city is calm and slow.

words.def: you hold it over your head in rain
a small place for drinks and food
animals with wings that can fly

questions.q: Where does Tom walk to?
What does Tom drink?
Why does Tom like rainy days?
questions.a: Because the city is calm and slow.

items.title: Mei Cooks Dinner in Tokyo
items.summary: Mei and her brother Ken cook, eat, and clean up together in Tokyo.
items.body: Mei comes home from work at six in the evening. Her kitchen in Tokyo is small but clean. She cooks rice, fish, and green vegetables for dinner. Her brother Ken arrives at seven. They eat together and talk about their day. After dinner, Mei washes the dishes and Ken dries them. Then they drink green tea and watch TV.

words.def: the room where you cook food
an animal that lives in water
a hot drink from green leaves

questions.q: When does Mei come home?
What does Mei cook for dinner?
What do Mei and Ken drink after dinner?

items.title: Kofi Works on a Farm
items.summary: Kofi cares for his animals and grows food on his farm near Nairobi.
items.body: Kofi has a small farm near Nairobi. Every morning he gives water to the chickens and the two brown cows. His dog Bulo runs with him to the fields. Kofi grows corn and beans. In the afternoon, he sits under a big tree and eats his lunch there. The weather is warm and the sky is blue. Kofi loves his quiet life on the farm.

words.def: a place with fields and animals
big farm animals that give milk
sun, rain, and wind in a place

questions.q: Where is Kofi's farm?
What animals live on the farm?
Where does Kofi eat his lunch?

items.title: Emma Studies at the Library
items.summary: Emma studies English and new words at the big library in Toronto.
items.body: Emma is a student in Toronto. On Saturdays she goes to the big library near the river. She takes her notebook, two pens, and a bottle of water. First she reads her English book. Then she writes ten new words in the notebook. A kind teacher helps her with the hard words. At four o'clock, Emma closes her books and goes home happy.

words.def: a place with many books to read
a person who studies at school
a person who helps you learn
a glass or plastic container for drinks

questions.q: Where does Emma go on Saturdays?
How many new words does Emma write?
Who helps Emma with hard words?

items.title: A Warm Day at the Beach
items.summary: Omar and his sister Dina enjoy a summer day at the beach in Alexandria.
items.body: Omar and his sister Dina go to the beach in Alexandria. The sand is hot under their feet. Dina puts her towel near an old white wall. Omar swims in the blue sea and then lies in the sun. They eat sandwiches and drink lemonade. In the evening, they watch the orange sunset over the water. It is a perfect summer day.

words.def: sandy land next to the sea
many very small stones on beaches

questions.q: Where do Omar and Dina go?
What does Omar do in the sea?
What do they watch in the evening?

items.title: Grace Grows Flowers and Herbs
items.summary: Grace cares for her garden of roses, sunflowers, and mint every morning.
items.body: Grace has a small garden behind her house. Every morning she checks her plants with a cup of tea in her hand. This year she grows red roses, yellow sunflowers, and fresh mint. Bees fly from flower to flower. Grace pulls the weeds and gives water to dry soil. Her neighbor says the garden looks beautiful. Grace feels proud when the first rose opens.

words.def: a place with flowers next to a house
small flying insects that make honey
wild plants that grow where you do not want
a green plant with a fresh smell

questions.q: What does Grace grow in her garden?
Which insects fly from flower to flower?
What does the neighbor say?

items.title: Ken Rides Along the River
items.summary: Ken enjoys a Sunday bicycle ride along the river in Seoul.
items.body: Ken rides his bicycle along the river in Seoul every Sunday. The path is long and safe. He passes bridges, parks, and small coffee shops. Many people run and skate there too. After one hour, Ken stops and buys a cold drink. He sits on a bench and watches the boats. Then he rides home before lunch. Cycling makes him strong and happy.

words.def: a two-wheel ride you push with feet

questions.q: Where does Ken ride his bicycle?
What does Ken buy after one hour?
How does cycling make Ken feel?

items.title: Amina Visits the Doctor
items.summary: Amina has a small cold, and the doctor in Cairo helps her feel better.
items.body: Amina does not feel well today. Her head hurts and her throat is sore. Her mother takes her to the doctor in Cairo. The doctor looks at her throat and asks some questions. He says it is only a small cold. Amina drinks warm tea with honey and rests for two days. She also takes her medicine and sleeps a lot. Soon she feels better.

words.def: a person who helps sick people
what you take to feel better
a small sickness with a runny nose

questions.q: Where does Amina's mother take her?
What does Amina drink?
How long does Amina rest?

items.title: Snow Falls in Ivan's City
items.summary: Ivan enjoys the first snow of winter in Warsaw with warm clothes and soup.
items.body: Ivan opens the window and sees snow for the first time this winter. The streets in Warsaw are white and quiet. He puts on his warm coat, a hat, and thick gloves. Children make a big snowman in the park. Ivan buys hot soup for lunch and takes photos of the trees. He sends the photos to his sister in Prague.

words.def: soft white water that falls in winter
a figure people make from snow

questions.q: What does Ivan see from the window?
What do the children make in the park?
Who receives Ivan's photos?

items.title: Fatou Works in a Bakery
items.summary: Fatou starts work early and makes fresh bread in a bakery in Dakar.
items.body: Fatou works in a small bakery in Dakar. She starts at five in the morning when the city is still dark. She makes bread, cakes, and sweet pastries. The smell of fresh bread fills the street. People come before work and buy warm loaves. Fatou knows many customers by name. At noon, her friend Awa brings her lunch and they sit together outside.

words.def: people who buy things in a shop

questions.q: Where does Fatou work?
questions.a: In a small bakery in Dakar.

questions.q: When does Fatou start work?
What does Awa bring Fatou?

items.title: A Night of Camping for Jack
items.summary: Jack and his cousin Sam camp for one night in the forest.
items.body: Jack and his cousin Sam camp in the forest for one night. They carry a green tent, sleeping bags, and food in big backpacks. Near the river, Jack puts up the tent while Sam collects dry wood. At night, they cook sausages on a small fire and look at the stars. The sky is full of bright stars. An owl sings in the tall trees.

words.def: bags you carry on your back
bright points of light at night
a bird that hunts at night
a big place full of trees

questions.q: Where do Jack and Sam camp?
What do they cook on the fire?
What animal sings in the trees?

items.title: Sofia Visits a Museum in Madrid
items.summary: Sofia and her cousin Pablo visit an old museum in Madrid.
items.body: Sofia takes the metro to the city center in Madrid. She meets her cousin Pablo in front of the old museum. Inside, they see paintings of kings, ships, and flowers. Sofia likes a picture of a sunny garden best. A guide explains the history of each painting. After two hours, they sit in the museum cafe and eat cake. The visit costs only three euros.

words.def: a place with old things to see
a person who shows you places
money used in many European countries

questions.q: How does Sofia travel to the city center?
What does Sofia like best?
questions.a: A picture of a sunny garden.

questions.q: How much does the visit cost?

items.title: Marco Drives a Boat in Venice
items.summary: Marco drives his boat with visitors along the canals of Venice.
items.body: Marco is a boat driver in Venice. He takes visitors along the narrow blue canals. This morning, a family from Japan sits in his boat. Marco points at the old bridge and the tall bell tower. The water shines in the sun. The family takes many photos and waves at people in other boats. At noon, Marco parks his boat and eats pasta near the water.

words.def: people who come to see a place

questions.q: What is Marco's job?
Where does the family sit?
What does Marco eat at noon?

items.title: Priya Shops at the Market
items.summary: Priya buys fresh vegetables at her local market in India every Tuesday.
items.body: Every Tuesday, Priya walks to the vegetable market in her town in India. She carries a large cloth bag. Today she buys tomatoes, onions, green beans, and a big bag of rice. The sellers call out their best prices. Priya checks the tomatoes carefully and picks the red ones. On the way home, she meets her neighbor and gives her two lemons.

questions.q: When does Priya go to the market?
What does Priya carry?
What does Priya give her neighbor?

items.title: Yuki Sees the Cherry Flowers
items.summary: Yuki enjoys the cherry flowers with her friend Hana in a park in Kyoto.
items.body: In spring, Yuki takes a train to the park in Kyoto. The cherry trees are full of pink flowers. Families sit on blankets under the trees and eat rice balls. Yuki takes off her shoes and walks on the soft grass. A light wind moves the petals. Her friend Hana plays a song on a guitar. They laugh, sing, and take photos until the evening.

words.def: the colored parts of a flower
warm covers for sitting on grass

questions.q: Where does Yuki go in spring?
What do families eat under the trees?
What does Hana play?

items.title: Khaled Starts a New Job
items.summary: Khaled starts a new job and meets his friendly team in Amman.
items.body: Khaled starts a new job at a small company in Amman. His desk is next to a wide window. On the first day, his manager shows him the kitchen, the meeting room, and the printer. Khaled meets his team and they drink coffee together. He writes his first email in the afternoon. At five, he goes home and tells his wife about the friendly people.

words.def: the boss of a team at work
the woman a man is married to

questions.q: Where does Khaled start a new job?
questions.a: At a small company in Amman.

questions.q: What does the manager show him?
questions.a: The kitchen, meeting room, and printer.

questions.q: What does Khaled tell his wife?

items.title: Zola Trains Her Dog Robo
items.summary: Zola trains her young dog Robo in the park in Cape Town.
items.body: Zola has a young dog called Robo. Every afternoon in Cape Town, she trains him in the park. She says sit, and Robo sits. She says stay, and he waits. When Robo does well, he gets a small treat. Zola also teaches him to bring her the ball. After one month, Robo can walk without a rope. The neighbors clap when Robo jumps over a low wall.

words.def: teaches an animal to do things
the flat side of a building

questions.q: What is the dog's name?
Where does Zola train Robo?
What does Robo get when he does well?

items.title: A Coffee for Elena
items.summary: Elena and Marta talk over coffee and cake in a Barcelona cafe.
items.body: On Friday evening, Elena and her friend Marta sit in a cafe in Barcelona. They order two cups of coffee and a piece of chocolate cake. Outside, people walk past with bags and bicycles. Elena talks about her new flat near the port. Marta shows photos of her cat on her phone. The sky turns pink, and a street musician plays a soft song nearby.

words.def: to ask for food in a cafe
a home in a big building

questions.q: What do Elena and Marta order?
What does Marta show on her phone?
Where is Elena's new flat?

items.title: Tariq Gets Ready for School
items.summary: Tariq gets ready for school and rides the bus in the morning.
items.body: Tariq gets up at half past six and opens the window. He washes his face with cold water and puts on his school clothes. In the kitchen, his father makes eggs and cheese sandwiches. Tariq eats quickly and drinks a glass of milk. He checks his school bag: books, pencils, and his sports shoes. At seven thirty, he rides the bus with his friend Rami.

words.def: food between two pieces of bread
a big car for many people

questions.q: What time does Tariq get up?
What does his father make?
How does Tariq go to school?

items.title: Lucy's Ninth Birthday Party
items.summary: Lucy celebrates her ninth birthday with family and friends in the garden.
items.body: Today is Lucy's ninth birthday. Her mother makes a big chocolate cake with white cream. Grandpa and Grandma arrive at four with colorful balloons. Lucy's friends play games in the garden and jump on the grass. They sing the birthday song, and Lucy closes her eyes and makes a wish. Then she cuts the cake. Everyone eats cake and ice cream in the warm sun.

words.def: colorful rubber balls full of air
the soft white part of milk

questions.q: Whose birthday is it?
What do Grandpa and Grandma bring?
What does Lucy do before cutting the cake?

items.title: Hassan Goes Fishing
items.summary: Hassan catches a big fish at the lake and lets it go free.
items.body: Hassan goes fishing at the lake every Thursday after work. He sits on a wooden box with his long fishing rod. The water is calm and the air smells of green plants. Hassan waits a long time. Suddenly, the line moves and he pulls hard. A big fish jumps out of the water. Hassan laughs and lets it go back into the lake.

words.def: a big area of still water
very fast and with no warning
an animal that lives in water

questions.q: When does Hassan go fishing?
Where does he sit?
What does Hassan do with the big fish?

items.title: Anna's Train to Istanbul
items.summary: Anna travels by train to Istanbul and meets a kind man on the way.
items.body: Anna travels by train from Sofia to Istanbul. The train crosses green hills and small villages. She sits next to an old man who reads a newspaper. They share bread and cheese and talk with simple words. After five hours, the train stops at a big station. Anna sees tall towers and busy streets. Her hotel is near the station. She is happy to arrive in a new city.

words.def: it runs on rails and carries people

questions.q: Where does Anna's train start?
What do Anna and the man share?
Where is Anna's hotel?

items.title: David Learns to Swim
items.summary: David learns to swim at the pool in Sydney with his coach.
items.body: David has a swimming lesson at the pool in Sydney every Monday. His coach, Miss Lee, stands in the water and shows the arm movements. David kicks his legs and holds a blue board. First he swims the short way, then the long way. Water goes in his mouth and he laughs. After the lesson, he showers and feels strong and hungry.

words.def: a person who teaches a sport
a place full of water for swimming
a flat piece of wood or plastic

questions.q: When is David's swimming lesson?
Who is David's coach?
How does David feel after the lesson?

items.title: Ordering Food at a Small Cafe
items.summary: A customer orders chicken and rice at a small cafe.
items.body: A: Good afternoon. What can I get you? B: Hello. Can I have chicken and rice, please? A: Sure. Anything to drink? B: An orange juice, please. A: Here you are. That is eight dollars. B: Thank you very much. A: Enjoy your meal! B: Thanks.

words.def: food you eat at one time

questions.q: What does the customer order?
How much is the meal?
What does the waiter say at the end?

items.title: At the Doctor's Office
items.summary: A doctor listens to a patient with a sore ear and gives medicine.
items.body: A: Good morning. What is the problem? B: My ear hurts and I feel very tired. A: When does it hurt most, in the day or at night? B: At night. I cannot sleep well. A: I see. You have a small infection. B: Oh no. Is it bad? A: No. Take this medicine twice a day. B: Thank you, doctor.

words.def: a small sickness in the body
what you take to feel better
something that is hard or wrong
to rest with closed eyes at night

questions.q: What is the problem?
When does the ear hurt most?
What does the doctor give?

items.title: Buying New Shoes at the Market
items.summary: A customer buys running shoes at the market with a seller's help.
items.body: A: Hello. Can I help you? B: Yes, please. I need new shoes for running. A: What is your size? B: Size forty, I think. A: Try these black ones. They are very light. B: They feel good. How much are they? A: Thirty dollars. B: Great. Here is the money.

words.def: you wear them on your feet

questions.q: What does the customer need?
What size does she need?
How much are the shoes?

items.title: Asking the Way to the Station
items.summary: A man asks the way to the train station and the ticket window.
items.body: A: Excuse me, where is the train station? B: Go straight and turn left at the bank. A: Is it far from here? B: No, it is only five minutes on foot. A: Thank you. And where can I buy a ticket? B: At the small window near the door. A: You are very kind. Thanks a lot. B: You are welcome. Have a good trip!

words.def: sixty of them make one hour
small paper that lets you travel
a journey from one place to another

questions.q: Where does the man want to go?
Where does he turn left?
Where can he buy a ticket?
questions.a: At the small window near the door.

items.title: Checking In at a Hotel
items.summary: Yuki checks in at a hotel for a stay of two nights.
items.body: A: Good evening. Do you have a reservation? B: Yes, a room for two nights. The name is Yuki Tanaka. A: Welcome, Ms Tanaka. Here is your key. Room twelve, first floor. B: Does the room have a window? A: Yes, and the restaurant is open until ten. B: What time is breakfast? A: From seven to ten in the morning. B: Perfect. Thank you.

words.def: a room kept for you before you come
a small metal thing that opens a door
a place where you buy meals
the first meal of the day
the dark hours of the day

questions.q: How many nights does Yuki stay?
What is her room number?
What time is breakfast?

items.title: A Phone Call About the Weekend
items.summary: Two friends make plans to play tennis on Saturday morning.
items.body: A: Hi Grace! Do you want to play tennis on Saturday? B: Hi! Yes, but only in the morning. I work in the afternoon. A: Perfect. Let's meet at the sports club at nine. B: OK. Do I need to bring balls? A: No, I have two new balls and cold water. B: Great. See you on Saturday! A: See you! Wear a hat because the sun is strong.

words.def: a ball game for two or four players
a place for sports and members
to come together at a place
to have clothes on your body
the time between noon and evening

questions.q: When do Grace and her friend play tennis?
Where do they meet?
questions.a: At the sports club at nine.

questions.q: What does Grace have two of?

items.title: Buying Medicine at the Pharmacy
items.summary: A customer buys medicine for a headache at the pharmacy.
items.body: A: Hello. I need something for a headache. B: Do you have a fever too? A: No fever, just a bad headache. B: Take this green box. One pill every six hours. A: How much is it? B: Five euros. A: Here you are. Thank you for your help. B: Get well soon!

words.def: a hot body when you are sick
money used in many European countries
to make things easier for someone

questions.q: What does the customer need?
How often does he take the pill?
How much does it cost?

items.title: Choosing Fruit at the Market
items.summary: A customer tastes sweet mangoes and buys two kilos at the market.
items.body: A: Good morning! These mangoes are very sweet today. B: Really? How much for one kilo? A: Four dollars for this big yellow kind. B: Can I try a small piece? A: Of course. Here, taste it. B: Mmm, delicious! I take two kilos, please. A: Wonderful. That is eight dollars. B: Thank you. See you next week!

words.def: to try food with the mouth
words that mean yes or surely

questions.q: How much are the mangoes?
What does the customer taste?
How many kilos does she buy?

items.title: A Question in English Class
items.summary: A student asks her teacher about the meaning of the word weather.
items.body: A: Excuse me, Miss. What does the word weather mean? B: It means the sun, the rain, and the wind in a place. A: Can you say it in a sentence, please? B: Yes. The weather is cold and windy today. A: Thank you. And how do we write it? B: W-E-A-T-H-E-R. Copy it three times at home. A: OK, Miss. Thank you very much.

words.def: sun, rain, and wind in a place
to be the idea of a word
to write the same thing again

questions.q: What does the word weather mean?
questions.a: The sun, rain, and wind in a place.

questions.q: How does the student copy the word?
What is the example sentence?
questions.a: The weather is cold and windy today.

items.title: Two Neighbors at the Bus Stop
items.summary: Two neighbors talk about the late bus and the city center.
items.body: A: The bus is late again this morning. B: Yes. I wait twenty minutes every day. A: Do you go to the city center? B: Yes, I work in a bookshop there. A: My daughter loves that bookshop. She buys a book every month. B: That is nice. Oh, look, the bus is coming now. A: Finally! Have a good day at work. B: You too. Bye!

words.def: the middle part of a city
at the end, after a long time

questions.q: How long does she wait for the bus?
Where does she work?
How often does the daughter buy a book?

items.title: Help at the Airport Desk
items.summary: A passenger checks in her suitcase and learns her gate at the airport.
items.body: A: Good morning. Can I see your passport, please? B: Here it is. I fly to Cairo at eleven. A: Thank you. Do you have any bags to check? B: Yes, this big blue suitcase. A: Put it here. It is twenty-three kilos. That is fine. B: Which gate is flight seven-oh-two? A: Gate nine. Boarding starts at half past ten. B: Thank you very much!

words.def: your travel paper with your name
a big bag for travel things
the door you use to get on a plane

questions.q: Where does the woman fly?
How many kilos is the suitcase?
Which gate is the flight?

items.title: A Simple Job Interview
items.summary: A cook answers simple questions in a job interview at a restaurant.
items.body: A: Tell me about yourself. B: I am a cook in a small hotel now. A: Why do you want this job? B: I love making food for people. Your restaurant is near my house. A: Can you start next Monday? B: Yes, I can. What time does the kitchen open? A: At ten in the morning. We cook lunch and dinner. B: Thank you very much.

words.def: a place where you buy meals
the room where you cook food

questions.q: What is the man's job now?
questions.a: He is a cook in a hotel.

questions.q: Why does he want the job?
questions.a: He loves making food for people.

questions.q: When can he start?

items.title: A Lost Bag on the Bus
items.summary: A passenger asks about her lost bag at the bus office.
items.body: A: Excuse me. I left my bag on the last bus. B: Can you describe it? A: It is a small brown bag with a red flower. B: What is inside? A: My books, my keys, and my water bottle. B: Good news. A driver has your bag now. A: Oh, wonderful! Where can I get it? B: At the lost and found office near platform two.

words.def: a container you carry things in
small metal things that open doors
to say what something looks like
a person who drives a car or bus
the place where you get on a train

questions.q: What did she lose?
What is inside the bag?
questions.a: Books, keys, and a water bottle.

questions.q: Where is the bag now?
questions.a: At the lost and found office.

items.title: Making Plans for a Picnic
items.summary: Two friends plan a picnic in the park for a sunny day.
items.body: A: The sky is blue. Let's have a picnic in the park! B: What a good idea! What do we need? A: Sandwiches, fruit, and a blanket. B: I can make sandwiches and bring water. A: Great. I bring apples and my new picnic mat. B: What time do we meet? A: At eleven, near the big fountain. B: Perfect. I hope the sun stays out all day!

words.def: a warm cover for beds or grass
a machine that pushes water up
a thin cover for the floor

questions.q: What do they plan?
What does B bring?
Where do they meet?
questions.a: Near the big fountain at eleven.

items.title: Facts About Water
items.summary: Simple facts about water and why our bodies need it every day.
items.body: Water is important for all people, animals, and plants. Our bodies need about eight cups of water every day. Water has no color, no smell, and no taste. It freezes at zero degrees and becomes ice. In hot weather, we lose water when we run or play, so we drink more water. Rivers, lakes, and seas hold most of the water on Earth.

words.def: water made very cold and hard
long waters that run to the sea

questions.q: How much water do our bodies need every day?
What does water become at zero degrees?
What holds most of the water on Earth?

items.title: The Sun and Our Days
items.summary: Facts about the sun, its light and heat, and being safe in the sun.
items.body: The sun is a very big star. It gives light and heat to our planet. Plants use sunlight to make their food. The sun rises in the east every morning and sets in the west. In summer, the days are long and hot. In winter, the nights are long and cold. Doctors say too much sun is bad for our skin.

words.def: a hot, bright point of light in the sky
a big round world in space
light that comes from the sun
the side where the sun comes up

questions.q: What does the sun give our planet?
Where does the sun rise?
Why is too much sun bad?
questions.a: It is bad for our skin.

items.title: Why Cats Are Good Pets
items.summary: Facts about cats as pets, their sleep, fur, and long lives.
items.body: Many families keep cats as pets. A cat sleeps for many hours every day, sometimes up to sixteen hours. Cats clean their fur with their tongues. They eat meat, so they catch mice and small birds. A happy cat makes a soft sound when you touch it. Cats use their whiskers to feel things in the dark. They can live for about fifteen years.

words.def: long hairs near a cat's mouth
the part of the mouth for taste
to take an animal with hands or tools

questions.q: How many hours does a cat sleep?
What do cats clean with their tongues?
How long can cats live?

items.title: The Apple: A Popular Fruit
items.summary: Facts about apples, where they grow, and how people eat them.
items.body: Apples grow on trees in many countries. The tree has white or pink flowers in spring. Apples can be red, green, or yellow. People eat them fresh, drink apple juice, or bake apple pies. An apple has many good things for the body. Farmers pick the fruit in autumn. Cool places are best for keeping apples fresh for a long time.

words.def: sweet baked food with fruit inside

questions.q: What colors can apples be?
When do farmers pick apples?
Where do apples grow?

items.title: Getting Around by Bus
items.summary: Facts about city buses, tickets, and why buses help the air.
items.body: In big cities, many people travel by bus. A city bus carries about eighty passengers. Passengers wait at bus stops and read the numbers on the front. You pay before you sit, or you tap a card when you get on. Buses are cheaper than cars and better for the air. At night, some cities have special night buses. Seats near the front are for older people.

words.def: people who travel in a bus or plane
what we take in through the nose

questions.q: How many passengers can a city bus carry?
Why are buses better than cars?
questions.a: They are cheaper and better for the air.

questions.q: Who sits near the front?

items.title: Bees Make Our Honey
items.summary: Facts about bees, their hives, and how they make honey.
items.body: Bees are small insects, but they do a big job. They fly from flower to flower and carry pollen. This helps plants make fruit and seeds. Bees live together in a hive with one queen. Worker bees make honey from the juice of flowers. Beekeepers wear special clothes and take the honey in summer. One jar of honey is the work of many bees.

words.def: the one female bee that lays eggs

questions.q: What do bees carry from flower to flower?
Where do bees live?
What do bees make honey from?

items.title: Penguins: Birds That Swim
items.summary: Facts about penguins, birds that cannot fly but swim very well.
items.body: Penguins are birds, but they cannot fly. Their wings work like fins in the water. Penguins swim fast and eat fish and small sea animals. They live in big groups, sometimes with thousands of birds. In cold places, penguins stand close together to stay warm. A mother penguin lays one or two eggs. Both parents keep the eggs safe and bring food for the chicks.

words.def: black and white birds that swim
many animals together in one place

questions.q: What do penguin wings work like?
What do penguins eat?
How many eggs does a mother penguin lay?

items.title: Trees Give Us Clean Air
items.summary: Facts about trees, their clean air, shade, and long lives.
items.body: Trees are important for every city and village. Their leaves take dirty air and give us clean air. Birds build nests in tall trees, and children play under them. In hot summers, trees give cool shade. Many trees lose their leaves in autumn, and new leaves grow in spring. People plant small trees in parks and streets. A tree can live for hundreds of years.

words.def: the green parts of a plant
to put in the ground to grow

questions.q: What do tree leaves give us?
What do birds build in trees?
Where do people plant small trees?

items.title: Good Sleep for Children
items.summary: Facts about good sleep for children and simple bedtime habits.
items.body: Children need about ten hours of sleep every night. Sleep helps the body grow and helps the brain learn new things. Doctors say no screens or games in bed. A dark, quiet room is best for good sleep. Try to sleep and wake up at the same time every day. A glass of warm milk before bed helps many people relax. Bad sleep makes you tired at school.

words.def: the part of the body that thinks

questions.q: How many hours of sleep do children need?
What is the best kind of room for sleep?
What helps many people relax before bed?

items.title: What You Find in a Library
items.summary: Facts about libraries, their books, and the work of the librarian.
items.body: A library is a quiet place full of books. People can read there for free and take books home for a few weeks. Libraries also have newspapers, maps, and computers. A librarian helps visitors find the right books. Many libraries have story time for small children on weekends. You can study at a big table or sit in a soft chair. Remember to bring the books back on time.

words.def: a person who works with books in a library
people who come to see a place
to keep something in your mind

questions.q: What can people take home from a library?
Who helps visitors find books?
What do many libraries have on weekends?

items.title: The Moon in the Night Sky
items.summary: Facts about the moon, its light, and visits by astronauts.
items.body: The moon goes around our planet once a month. At night, it gives soft light. The moon has no light; the sun lights it. There is no air or water on the moon, so nothing grows there. Astronauts ride rockets to visit the moon and walk on its gray dust. Some nights the moon looks round and full. On other nights, we see only a thin piece.

words.def: the bright thing in the night sky
very small pieces of dry earth
a big round world in space

questions.q: How often does the moon go around our planet?
What is not on the moon?
How do astronauts travel to the moon?

items.title: Life in the Desert
items.summary: Facts about deserts, their dry weather, plants, and animals.
items.body: A desert is a very dry place with little rain. Some deserts are hot in the day and cold at night. Sand covers many deserts, but some have rocks and dry hills. Only special plants grow there, like the cactus, which holds water inside. Camels carry people and things across the sand. Many desert animals come out only at night when it is cool.

words.def: a very dry place with little rain
a green desert plant with sharp points
big desert animals with one or two humps
many very small stones on beaches

questions.q: What is a desert like?
Which plant holds water inside?
When do desert animals come out?

items.title: Bicycles: A Good Way to Travel
items.summary: Facts about bicycles, how they work, and why they are good.
items.body: A bicycle has two wheels, a seat, and two pedals. You push the pedals with your feet, and the wheels turn. Many people ride bikes to work or school because they are cheap and clean. Bicycles use no fuel and make no smoke, so they are good for the air. Wear a helmet to keep your head safe. In some cities, you can rent a bike near the station.

words.def: round parts that turn and roll
foot parts you push to ride
to pay money to use something
material that gives power to cars

questions.q: What does a bicycle have?
questions.a: Two wheels, a seat, and two pedals.

questions.q: Why are bicycles good for the air?
questions.a: They use no fuel and make no smoke.

questions.q: What do you wear to keep your head safe?

items.title: The Four Seasons of the Year
items.summary: Facts about the four seasons and the weather of each one.
items.body: In many countries, the year has four seasons. Spring brings warm weather and new flowers. Summer is the hottest season, and children play outside until late. In autumn, leaves change color and fall from the trees. Winter is the coldest season, with short days and long nights. Some places have rain in winter and snow on the mountains. Every season has its own beauty.

words.def: the four parts of the year
very high land with rocks and trees

questions.q: How many seasons does the year have?
What happens to leaves in autumn?
Where does snow fall?

items.title: My Daily Routine
items.summary: Write about your daily routine.
items.body: I get up at seven o'clock every morning. First, I wash my face and eat breakfast with my family. I usually have bread, cheese, and tea. Then I go to school by bus. My classes start at eight. After school, I do my homework and play football with my friends. In the evening, I have dinner and read a book. I go to bed at ten.

words.def: the first meal of the day
school work you do at home
a team game with a big ball

questions.q: What does the writer eat for breakfast?
How does the writer go to school?
What time does the writer go to bed?

items.title: My Favorite Food
items.summary: Write about your favorite food.
items.body: My favorite food is rice with chicken and vegetables. My mother cooks it on Friday, and the whole family eats together. The rice is soft and the chicken is delicious. We also eat a green salad with tomatoes and lemon. After lunch, I help my mother wash the dishes. Sometimes we eat fruit for dessert. I love this food because it tastes like home.

questions.q: What is the writer's favorite food?
When does the mother cook it?
What do they eat for dessert?

items.title: My Family
items.summary: Write about your family.
items.body: There are five people in my family: my father, my mother, two brothers, and me. My father works in a bank, and my mother teaches music at a school. My big brother plays basketball, and my little brother draws pictures. We eat dinner together every evening and talk about our day. On Fridays, we visit our grandparents. I love my family very much.

words.def: a place that keeps money safe
the mother and father of your parents
a game with a big orange ball
boys with the same parents as you

questions.q: How many people are in the family?
Where does the father work?
What does the big brother play?

items.title: My Town
items.summary: Write about your town or city.
items.body: I live in a small town by the sea. There are two schools, a market, and a big park with a fountain. In summer, many visitors come to swim and eat ice cream by the port. The streets are clean and the people are friendly. My favorite place is the library, because I can read and study there. I think my town is a wonderful place to live.

questions.q: Where is the writer's town?
What do visitors do in summer?
What is the writer's favorite place?

items.title: My Best Friend
items.summary: Write about your best friend.
items.body: My best friend is called Nadia. We are the same age and we sit together at school. Nadia is funny and kind. She always shares her food with me and helps me with math. After school, we ride our bikes in the park or listen to music. When I feel sad, she makes me laugh. I hope we stay friends for many years.

words.def: the happy sound when something is funny

questions.q: What is the friend's name?
What does Nadia help with?
What do they do after school?
questions.a: Ride bikes or listen to music.

items.title: My Weekend Plans
items.summary: Write about your weekend plans.
items.body: On Saturday morning, I clean my room and finish my homework. In the afternoon, my cousin comes to our house and we watch a film. On Sunday, my family and I go to the park for a picnic. I take my new ball and my camera and take photos of the ducks. In the evening, I prepare my bag for school. Weekends are short, but I love them.

words.def: a story you watch on a screen
child of your aunt or uncle

questions.q: What does the writer do on Saturday morning?
questions.a: Cleans her room and finishes homework.

questions.q: Where does the family go on Sunday?
questions.a: To the park for a picnic.

questions.q: What does the writer photograph?

items.title: My House
items.summary: Write about your house or flat.
items.body: My family lives in a small flat on the third floor. It has two bedrooms, a kitchen, a bathroom, and a living room. My bedroom has a bed, a desk, and a window with orange curtains. I keep my books on a wooden shelf. In the living room, we watch TV and drink tea together. There is a small balcony with flowers in the summer.

words.def: a small outside place on a high floor

questions.q: Which floor does the family live on?
What color are the curtains?
Where do the books stay?

items.title: My Hobby: Drawing
items.summary: Write about your favorite hobby.
items.body: My favorite hobby is drawing. I draw animals, houses, and people from my street. Every Friday, I sit near the window with my pencils and a thick notebook. My mother says my cats look real. My teacher puts my best pictures on the wall of our classroom. Drawing makes me calm and happy. One day, I want to draw a big book for children.

words.def: making pictures with a pen or pencil
a fun activity you do often
wooden tools for writing and drawing
the flat side of a room

questions.q: What is the writer's hobby?
What does the writer draw?
Where do the best pictures go?
